Innventure is a company-creation platform. Accelsius is the economic center of gravity. Consolidated revenue was about $1.4 million in the March 2026 quarter, with about $55 million of unrestricted cash and a large net loss. The equity story is an asset claim on Accelsius (and smaller options in AeroFlexx and Refinity)
At today's price, we expect about **11.9%** per year over five years on the base case.
*Primary risk: Accelsius adoption stalls while the parent burns cash and dilutes.
Capital markets risk: shelf registrations and preferred structures can reprice ownership of the upside.
Technology / competitive risk: OEMs with distribution may catch up even if Accelsius is ahead today.

Competition in cards and BNPL from Mercado Pago is real and intensifying; Sea’s Monee is a fast but still small Brazil credit book. We normalize growth well below last year’s 4

*Primary risk: Marketplace lenders (especially Mercado Pago) use commerce data to take credit-card and BNPL share while Open Finance makes balances easier to move, compressing Nu’s risk-adjusted growth.
1. Credit competition / data: Mercado Pago (and later Monee) use commerce graphs to originate cards and BNPL cheaper; Open Finance helps rivals peel credit.
2. Credit cycle: NPL 6.6% already elevated vs pristine books; low-and-grow strategy can look wrong in a downturn.

Single-country Poland exposure (FX, regulation, consumer).
CapEx intensity: if openings miss returns, accounting FCF stays depressed longer than modeled.

claim_ledger.claim: Amazon runs four reinforcing engines: retail logistics density, AWS, high-margin advertising (more than $70 billion trailing twelve months), and custom silicon (Trainium, Graviton, Nitro). Q1 2026 consolidated operating income $23.9 billion (+30%) and AWS re-acceleration (+28%) confirm operating momentum. [Fact] Traili

*Primary risk: Prolonged AI capital spending overshoot (trailing purchases $147.3 billion vs operating cash flow $148.5 billion) without AWS, ads, and silicon returns showing up in normalized free cash flow per share.
AWS growth deceleration and margin compression from hyperscaler price competition.
Regulatory/antitrust on retail or cloud.

Allegion is a branded security and access-control compounder trading near fair value on a filing-grounded component schedule. Normalized owner cash is $7.96 per share (FY2025 cash from operations minus capital spending, divided by ~86.1 million shares). At $138.13 (Yahoo close 2026-07-20), Lawrence base case implies 13
We expect **13.4%** per year over 7 years at **~$138.13** on **$7.96 per share** starting owner cash (Lawrence base case).
*Primary risk: Non-residential construction slowdown compresses volumes and delays electronic upgrade cycles, while fixed debt service persists.
Leverage: $1.98 billion long-term debt versus $356 million cash (~$19 per share net claim drag in component schedule).
International margin gap: International segment ~9% operating margin vs Americas ~28% limits consolidated mix improvement if Americas slows.

Ameren is a Midwest regulated utility investing heavily in transmission, distribution, and renewables across Missouri and Illinois. FY2025 diluted earnings were $5.35 per share on $8.8 billion of revenue, and the board raised the annual dividend to $3.00 per share in February 2026. At $113.78 per share, Marvin's Lawren
*Primary risk: Regulatory and political pushback slows capex recovery or forces equity-heavy financing, diluting per-share growth below the capital plan.
If Illinois MYRP appeals reduce allowed returns or capital trackers, Illinois earnings stall.
If Missouri affordability politics cap ROE or disallow PISA investments, Missouri growth slows.

ADM is a scale ag processor and origination network trading at roughly fair value on a filing-grounded component schedule. Normalized owner cash is $6.50 per share (operating cash flow minus an estimated maintenance and growth capital spending haircut). At $85.67 (Yahoo close 2026-07-20), Lawrence base case implies 12.
We expect **12.4%** per year over 7 years at **~$85.67** on **$6.50 per share** starting owner cash (Lawrence base case).
*Primary risk: Crush-margin compression and global trade disruption (especially China soybean/meal flows) reduce owner cash faster than origination scale can offset.
Leverage: $6.6 billion long-term debt versus $1.0 billion cash limits dhando in a prolonged trough.
Governance: SEC settlement closed the intersegment investigation, but control and reporting credibility remain a human review item.

C3.ai is an enterprise AI application platform in a revenue trough: FY2026 sales fell to $227.1 million from $327.6 million, while the balance sheet still carries $66.2 million cash and no term debt. Normalized owner cash is modeled at $0.80 per share [Assumption] after reinvestment and stock-based compensation adjustm
We expect **36.55%** per year over 7 years at **$8.61** on **$0.80/sh** starting owner cash (synthesis base).
*Primary risk: Enterprise AI spending shifts to hyperscaler-native tools, compressing C3.ai win rates and pricing before the revenue trough ends.
Revenue trajectory: FY2026 -31% decline may extend if large deals slip or churn rises.
Dilution and SBC: Stock-based compensation and equity issuance erode per-share owner cash (`cycle_reserve` -$1.50/sh base).

Valuation: Spot $309.09 vs $84.20/sh contract base leaves large downside if growth normalizes (`valuation_contract.json`).
Insider selling: Negligible ICS; executives monetizing at elevated prices (`insider_signal_2026-07-25.md`).

*Primary risk: M&A indiscipline; goodwill impairment SEK 73M (Q3 2025); equity ratio 42.8% and falling.

*Primary risk: Prolonged slump in cash-equity turnover and China-linked flow after the FY2024–FY2025 boom, compressing trading fees and clearing balances.

The Steel Promissory Note is secured by all company assets; if it is not repaid or converted on favorable terms, equity could be wiped out in a formal wind-down.

Specialist consensus (>50% biotech funds) is the primary biotech quality screen.
Prefer names owned by multiple specialists; unique single-fund ideas underperform consensus.
Traditional P/E value is inverted in biotech; use spend vs market cap instead.
Own-price momentum is inverted; use clinical peer-cohort momentum.
Insider buys matter when non-CEO (especially CFO); sells are mostly noise.
Short interest identifies losers; size shorts for diversification, not conviction.
13F lag is acceptable because specialist holds are multi-year and illiquid in small caps.
Small-cap specialist concentration carries more return than large-cap specialist dollars.
Blended quality + spend value + peer momentum spreads returns more than any single factor.
Biotech quant is an overlay; it does not replace Lawrence IRR for compounders.
